# Supermatter Structural Recovery
When the Supermatter Crystal becomes damaged, microscopic fractures form within its structure.
These fractures expose new layers of the crystal, causing damaged material to separate and decompose.
This decomposition releases gaseous byproducts, primarily oxygen and tritium.
The Supermatter demonstrates a natural self-repairing behaviour, gradually closing these structural imperfections over time.
The mechanism behind this regenerative process is not fully understood.
Current research suggests the crystal actively reorganizes its internal structure to restore stability.
